question: A concave mirror forms a real image of three times the size of an object on a screen. The object and screen are then moved until the image is six times the size of the object. If the shift of the screen is 39 cm, then the focal length of the mirror is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**13 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Given**: A concave mirror forms a real image 3 times the size of the object, we have m₁=3 and v₁=3u₁.

**Formula**: (1)/(f)=(1)/(u)+(1)/(v)

**Given**: m₂=6, the new image distance v₂=6u₂, and the screen shift v₂-v₂=39cm

We solve the system of equations to find f:

From v₁=3u₁: (1)/(f)=(1)/(3u₁)+(1)/(u₁)=(4)/(3u₁), Thus u₁=(4f)/(3)

From v₂=6u₂: (1)/(f)=(1)/(6u₂)+(1)/(u₂)=(7)/(6u₂), Thus u₂=(7f)/(6)

Using v₂-v₁=39: 6u₂-3u₁=39.

Substituting u₁ and u₂: 6times (7f)/(6)-3times(4f)/(3)=39, which simplifies to 7f-4f=39.

Hence, 3f=39, and f=13cm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Concave Mirror:**

 
 
• A concave mirror, or converging mirror, has a reflecting surface that curves inward like the inside of a sphere.
 
• It converges light to a focal point, making it useful for focusing light and forming real images.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):**
 
 
• Magnification is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object.
 
• For mirrors, it is also given by the ratio of the image distance to the object distance (m=-(v)/(u)).
 
 
 
• **Mirror Formula:**
